value.author: samMularczyk
value.layerInfo: Chrome, smoke or heat, shaped by the layer's own alpha.

material: Which shading head runs over the shape field. The field itself is built the same way for all three.
spread: How far the shape field reaches, in pixels. This is the falloff distance that upstream gets by normalising against the whole image - as a control it is better, because a thick stroke and a thin one on the same layer both read correctly instead of being scaled against each other.
contourAmount: How hard the field bends the material at the silhouette. Low leaves the pattern flat across the shape; high crowds it against the edges, which is what makes the surface look like it wraps the form.
repetition: How many light/dark bands the stripe field repeats. Think of it as how tightly banded the environment being reflected is.
softness: Edge softness of each band. Zero gives hard chrome; higher gives a brushed or satin surface.
shiftRed: Phase offset of the red channel against green. Together with Blue Shift this is the entire chromatic aberration - three samples of one field at three offsets, which is why the fringing follows the strokes and not the frame.
shiftBlue: Phase offset of the blue channel. Negative swaps which side of an edge goes warm.
distortion: Noise added into the field before it warps the bands, so the reflection ripples rather than sitting still. On Heat this doubles as the dither amount.
metalAngle: Direction of the band ramp, in degrees. Also rotates Smoke's warp and Heat's scrolling band.
tintColor: Colour applied with a colour burn rather than a multiply, so the highlights stay near white while the darks take the colour - which is what separates tinted metal from a merely coloured object. Alpha is the amount.
innerDistortion: Warp strength inside the shape. This one is multiplied by the field, so it is calm at the rim and strongest through the thick of the form - that contrast is the whole gem impression.
outerDistortion: Warp strength of the smoke outside the shape, which is not tied to the field.
innerGlow: Brightness of the material inside the shape. On Heat this is the heat of the body; on Smoke it is how strongly the plume shows through the silhouette.
outerGlow: Brightness of the halo outside the shape. Needs Spread to have room - the layer bounds expand to match, so a big halo costs padding.
smokeScale: Size of the smoke plume. Lower zooms out and, because the warp is damped where it would alias, also calms it.
smokeSpill: How far the plume is allowed from the shape. At zero it is confined to the falloff measured from the layer's own alpha, so the smoke pours off the form; at one it fills the layer's bounds, which is what the reference does because there the shader IS the whole frame. It always fades out before the padded edge either way.
smokeInner: Colour filling the shape behind the smoke.
heat1: First stop of the ramp. Low values of the field land here.
heatCount: How many stops of the ramp are used.
speed: Rate the pattern moves. Zero freezes it.
backColor: Colour behind the result. Transparent by default so it composites over whatever is beneath.
amount: Mix between the original layer and the result.
padding: Extra pixels of room around the layer for the effect to spread into. Cavalry 2.8 sizes this automatically; on 2.7.2 raise it by hand if the result clips at the layer bounds.
